 * opaque string, so it is reused directly rather than hashed again.
 */
function promptCacheKeyFor(sessionId: string): string {
  return sessionId
}

/** Request-local fallback; never infer a human turn identity from message history. */
function turnKeyFor(sessionId: string): string {
  // The harness passes no turn id, and no property of the request identifies a
  // turn reliably: the same user text recurs across turns, a tool result also
  // carries a user role, and the number of tool calls is 0 at the start of every
  // turn. Guessing here is what puts a routing token from one turn into the next,
  // which is the contract violation the header forbids.
  //
  // So the key is per request, not per turn. The cost is a full resend for the
  // rare follow-up inside one turn; the benefit is that no request can ever carry
  // another turn's state. Until the harness supplies a turn id this is the only
  // identity that cannot be wrong.
  const digest = createHash('sha256')
    .update(sessionId)
    .update('\0')
    .update(String(perRequestNonce()))
    .digest('hex')
    .slice(0, 24)
  return `${sessionId}#${digest}`
}

/** A value no two requests in this process share. */
let requestCounter = 0
function perRequestNonce(): number {
  requestCounter += 1
  return requestCounter
}

interface ToolState {
  index: number
  id: string
  itemId?: string
  name: string
  arguments: string
  started: boolean
}

export async function* parseResponsesStream(
  response: Response,
  signal?: AbortSignal,
  /** Kept for the public parser's positional compatibility; native arguments are never stripped. */
  _legacyHiddenSandboxControls: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(),
  /** Reports transport activity so a caller-side idle watchdog keeps rearming. */
  activity?: StreamActivity,
): AsyncIterable<StreamChunk> {
  if (response.body === null) throw new LlmError('Codex returned no response stream.', 'PROVIDER_ERROR')
  const reader = response.body.getReader()
  const abortReader = (): void => { void reader.cancel(signal?.reason).catch(() => undefined) }
  signal?.addEventListener('abort', abortReader, { once: true })
  const decoder = new TextDecoder()
  let buffer = ''
  let nextIndex = 0
  let textIndex: number | null = null
  let reasoningIndex: number | null = null
  let text = ''
  let reasoning = ''
  let pendingReasoningDelta = ''
  let reasoningTruncated = false
  let terminal: FinishReason | null = null
  /** Whether the terminal event was an incomplete response, whatever it maps to. */
  let terminalIncomplete = false
  let usage: TokenUsage | null = null
  let replayOutput: Array<Record<string, unknown>> = []
  const tools = new Map<string, ToolState>()

  const toolFor = (event: Record<string, unknown>, item?: Record<string, unknown>): ToolState => {
    const itemId = string(event.item_id) ?? string(item?.id)
    const outputIndex = number(event.output_index)
    const key = itemId ?? (outputIndex === undefined ? `tool-${tools.size}` : `index-${outputIndex}`)
    let tool = tools.get(key)
    if (tool === undefined) {
      tool = {
        index: nextIndex++,
        id: acceptIdentity(`call_${key}`, item?.call_id ?? event.call_id),
        itemId,
        name: acceptIdentity('', item?.name ?? event.name),
        arguments: '',
        started: false,
      }
      tools.set(key, tool)
    }
    return tool
  }

  /**
   * Adopt the complete answer text when the backend carries it only in terminal
   * events instead of `response.output_text.delta`. Deltas own the text when they
   * arrive: this is a no-op once a text block started, so a normally streamed
   * response never doubles its answer.
   * @param full - the complete text the terminal event carries.
   * @returns the chunks that make it a visible text block, or none.
   */
  const adoptText = (full: string): StreamChunk[] => {
    if (textIndex !== null || full === '') return []
    textIndex = nextIndex++
    text = full
    return [
      { type: 'block-start', index: textIndex, blockType: 'text' },
      { type: 'text-delta', index: textIndex, text: full },
    ]
  }

  const consume = async function* (event: Record<string, unknown>): AsyncIterable<StreamChunk> {
    const type = string(event.type)
    if (type === 'response.output_text.delta' || type === 'response.refusal.delta') {
      const delta = string(event.delta) ?? ''
      if (textIndex === null) {
        textIndex = nextIndex++
        yield { type: 'block-start', index: textIndex, blockType: 'text' }
      }
      text += delta
      if (delta) yield { type: 'text-delta', index: textIndex, text: delta }
      return
    }
    if (type === 'response.output_text.done') {
      yield* adoptText(string(event.text) ?? '')
      return
    }
    if (type === 'response.content_part.done') {
      const part = record(event.part)
      const partType = string(part?.type)
      if (partType === 'output_text' || partType === 'refusal') {
        yield* adoptText(string(part?.text) ?? '')
      }
      return
    }
    if (type === 'response.reasoning_summary_text.delta') {
      const delta = string(event.delta) ?? ''
      if (reasoningIndex === null) {
        reasoningIndex = nextIndex++
        yield { type: 'block-start', index: reasoningIndex, blockType: 'reasoning' }
      }
      const visibleDelta = visibleReasoningDelta(delta, reasoning.length, reasoningTruncated)
      reasoningTruncated ||= visibleDelta.truncated
      if (visibleDelta.text !== '') {
        reasoning += visibleDelta.text
        pendingReasoningDelta += visibleDelta.text
      }
      if (pendingReasoningDelta.length >= REASONING_DELTA_FLUSH_CHARS) {
        yield { type: 'reasoning-delta', index: reasoningIndex, text: pendingReasoningDelta }
        pendingReasoningDelta = ''
      }
      return
    }
    if (type === 'response.output_item.added' || type === 'response.output_item.done') {
      const item = record(event.item)
      if (item !== null && type === 'response.output_item.done') replayOutput.push(structuredClone(item))
      if (string(item?.type) !== 'function_call') {
        if (type === 'response.output_item.done') yield* adoptText(messageItemText(item))
        return
      }
      const tool = toolFor(event, item ?? undefined)
      tool.id = acceptIdentity(tool.id, item?.call_id)
      tool.name = acceptIdentity(tool.name, item?.name)
      const initial = string(item?.arguments) ?? ''
      if (!tool.started) {
        tool.started = true
        yield { type: 'block-start', index: tool.index, blockType: 'tool-call' }
        yield {
          type: 'tool-call-delta',
          index: tool.index,
          id: toToolCallId(tool.id),
          name: tool.name || undefined,
          argumentsDelta: initial,
        }
        tool.arguments = initial
      } else if (type === 'response.output_item.done' && initial !== '') {
        tool.arguments = initial
      }
      return
    }
    if (type === 'response.function_call_arguments.delta') {
      const tool = toolFor(event)
      tool.id = acceptIdentity(tool.id, event.call_id)
      tool.name = acceptIdentity(tool.name, event.name)
      const delta = string(event.delta) ?? ''
      if (!tool.started) {
        tool.started = true
        yield { type: 'block-start', index: tool.index, blockType: 'tool-call' }
      }
      tool.arguments += delta
      yield {
        type: 'tool-call-delta',
        index: tool.index,
        id: toToolCallId(tool.id),
        name: tool.name || undefined,
        argumentsDelta: delta,
      }
      return
    }
    if (type === 'response.function_call_arguments.done') {
      const tool = toolFor(event)
      tool.id = acceptIdentity(tool.id, event.call_id)
      tool.name = acceptIdentity(tool.name, event.name)
      const finalArguments = string(event.arguments)
      if (finalArguments !== undefined) tool.arguments = finalArguments
      return
    }
    if (type === 'response.completed' || type === 'response.incomplete') {
      const completed = record(event.response)
      usage = mapUsage(record(completed?.usage))
      const output = completed?.output
      if (Array.isArray(output)) {
        replayOutput = output.filter((item): item is Record<string, unknown> => record(item) !== null)
          .map((item) => structuredClone(item))
        for (const item of output) yield* adoptText(messageItemText(record(item)))
      }
      if (type === 'response.incomplete') {
        terminalIncomplete = true
        terminal = incompleteFinishReason(completed)
      } else {
        terminal = { kind: 'stop' }
      }
      return
    }
    if (type === 'response.failed' || type === 'error') {
      const error = record(event.error) ?? record(record(event.response)?.error)
      const message = string(error?.message) ?? 'Codex generation failed.'
      const rawCode = string(error?.code)?.toLowerCase()
      const isOverload = message.toLowerCase().includes('overload')
        || message.toLowerCase().includes('server error')
        || rawCode === 'server_error'
        || rawCode === 'service_unavailable'
        || rawCode === 'internal_error'
      const isRateLimit = message.toLowerCase().includes('rate limit') || rawCode === 'rate_limit'
      const code = isRateLimit ? 'RATE_LIMIT' : (isOverload ? 'SERVER_ERROR'
        : isContextOverflow(error) ? CONTEXT_OVERFLOW_CODE : (string(error?.code)?.toUpperCase() ?? 'PROVIDER_ERROR'))
      throw new LlmError(message, code)
    }
  }

  try {
    while (true) {
      if (signal?.aborted) throw signal.reason ?? new DOMException('Aborted', 'AbortError')
      const { done, value } = await reader.read()
      if (done) break
      // Bytes arriving at all prove the connection is alive, whatever the parser
      // makes of them; a byte-less read is not evidence of anything.
      if (value !== undefined && value.byteLength > 0) activity?.pulse()
      buffer += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true })
      const frames = buffer.split(/\r?\n\r?\n/)
      buffer = frames.pop() ?? ''
      for (const frame of frames) {
        // Counted per complete frame, before the `data:` filter below: a bare
        // comment heartbeat such as `: ping` yields no payload and is filtered
        // out, yet it is the clearest possible proof the upstream is still there.
        activity?.pulse()
        const data = frame.split(/\r?\n/)
          .filter((line) => line.startsWith('data:'))
          .map((line) => line.slice(5).trimStart())
          .join('\n')
        if (data === '' || data === '[DONE]') continue
        let event: unknown
        try {
          event = JSON.parse(data)
        } catch {
          throw new LlmError('Codex returned malformed streaming JSON.', 'PROTOCOL_ERROR')
        }
        const valueRecord = record(event)
        if (valueRecord !== null) yield* consume(valueRecord)
      }
    }
  } finally {
    signal?.removeEventListener('abort', abortReader)
    reader.releaseLock()
  }

  if (signal?.aborted) throw signal.reason ?? new DOMException('Aborted', 'AbortError')
  if (terminal === null) throw new LlmError('Codex stream ended before a terminal event.', 'PROTOCOL_ERROR')
  // consume() owns terminal assignments; TypeScript does not follow that closure.
  const finalReason = terminal as FinishReason
  if (reasoningIndex !== null) {
    if (pendingReasoningDelta !== '') {
      yield { type: 'reasoning-delta', index: reasoningIndex, text: pendingReasoningDelta }
      pendingReasoningDelta = ''
    }
    yield { type: 'block-end', index: reasoningIndex, block: { type: 'reasoning', text: reasoning } }
  }
  if (textIndex !== null) {
    yield { type: 'block-end', index: textIndex, block: { type: 'text', text } }
  }
  if (terminalIncomplete) {
    // An incomplete response must neither execute a finished-looking tool call
    // nor replay an unanswered call on the next request. Leave streamed tool
    // blocks unfinished so the harness drops them at the finish. This holds for
    // every incomplete reason, including a steered turn that finishes as a
    // plain stop: the turn was cut short, so its tool calls are unanswered.
    tools.clear()
    replayOutput = replayOutput.filter((item) => item.type !== 'function_call')
  }
  let validToolCount = 0
  const replayedToolCallIds = new Set(replayOutput.flatMap((item) => (
    item.type === 'function_call' && typeof item.call_id === 'string' ? [item.call_id] : []
  )))
  for (const tool of tools.values()) {
    if (!tool.started) continue
    if (!isSafeJsonArguments(tool.arguments) || tool.name === '') {
      throw new LlmError(`Codex returned invalid JSON arguments for tool ${tool.name || '(unnamed)'}.`, 'INVALID_TOOL_ARGUMENTS')
    }
    validToolCount++
    if (!replayedToolCallIds.has(tool.id)) {
      replayOutput.push({
        type: 'function_call',
        call_id: tool.id,
        name: tool.name,
        arguments: tool.arguments,
      })
      replayedToolCallIds.add(tool.id)
    }
    yield {
      type: 'block-end',
      index: tool.index,
      block: { type: 'tool-call', id: toToolCallId(tool.id), name: tool.name, arguments: tool.arguments },
    }
  }
  if (usage !== null) yield { type: 'usage', usage }
  yield {
    type: 'finish',
    reason: validToolCount > 0 ? { kind: 'tool-calls' } : finalReason,
    replayState: { response: { outputItems: replayOutput } },
  }
}

/**
 * The finish reason an incomplete response maps to.
 *
 * The provider states why it stopped in `incomplete_details.reason`, and the
 * reasons are not interchangeable:
 *
 * - A budget exhaustion (`max_output_tokens`, `max_messages`) is the
 *   truncated answer, so it is a max-tokens finish. A response that names no
 *   reason at all is treated the same way: the turn was cut short by an
 *   output limit far more often than by anything else, and reporting it as a
 *   normal stop would silently claim the answer was complete.
 * - A `steered` turn is one the user interrupted. Nothing failed, so it
 *   finishes as an ordinary stop.
 * - A `content_filter` is the provider's own refusal and keeps its own code.
 * - Any other reason is an unknown provider condition. It is reported as an
 *   incomplete provider failure with the raw reason and message preserved, so
 *   the report says what actually happened instead of naming a guess.
 */
function incompleteFinishReason(response: Record<string, unknown> | null): FinishReason {
  const details = record(response?.incomplete_details)
  const reason = details === null ? undefined : details.reason
  if (reason === undefined || reason === null
    || reason === 'max_output_tokens' || reason === 'max_messages') return { kind: 'max-tokens' }
  if (reason === 'steered') return { kind: 'stop' }
  const detail = JSON.stringify(reason)
  const message = string(record(response?.error)?.message)
  throw new LlmError(
    `Codex returned an incomplete response (${detail})${message ? `: ${message}` : '.'}`,
    reason === 'content_filter' ? 'CONTENT_FILTER' : 'PROVIDER_INCOMPLETE',
  )
}

function visibleReasoningDelta(
  delta: string,
  currentVisibleChars: number,
  alreadyTruncated: boolean,
): { text: string; truncated: boolean } {
  if (delta === '' || alreadyTruncated) return { text: '', truncated: alreadyTruncated }
  const remaining = MAX_VISIBLE_REASONING_CHARS - currentVisibleChars
  if (remaining <= 0) return { text: REASONING_TRUNCATED_NOTICE, truncated: true }
  if (delta.length <= remaining) return { text: delta, truncated: false }
  return { text: `${delta.slice(0, remaining)}${REASONING_TRUNCATED_NOTICE}`, truncated: true }
}

/**
 * Map one response's usage onto DSH's disjoint accounting.
 *
 * `input_tokens` is the whole input, so cached input has to be subtracted out of
 * it and reported on its own field. Cache WRITES are counted separately from
 * reads and billed separately: leaving a write inside `inputTokens` would make a
 * cold prefix look cheaper than it was and hide the cost of a write. A field the
 * service omits is unknown, not zero, so it is simply not reported.
 */
function mapUsage(value: Record<string, unknown> | null): TokenUsage | null {
  if (value === null) return null
  const totalInput = number(value.input_tokens) ?? 0
  const outputTokens = number(value.output_tokens) ?? 0
  const details = record(value.input_tokens_details)
  const cached = number(details?.cached_tokens)
  const written = number(details?.cache_write_tokens)
  const reasoning = number(record(value.output_tokens_details)?.reasoning_tokens)
  return {
    inputTokens: Math.max(0, totalInput - (cached ?? 0) - (written ?? 0)),
    outputTokens,
    ...(cached === undefined ? {} : { cacheReadTokens: cached }),
    ...(written === undefined ? {} : { cacheWriteTokens: written }),
    ...(reasoning === undefined ? {} : { reasoningTokens: reasoning }),
  }
}

function isSafeJsonArguments(value: string): boolean {
  try {
    const parsed = JSON.parse(value) as unknown
    return typeof parsed === 'object' && parsed !== null && !Array.isArray(parsed)
  } catch {
    return false
  }
}

async function responseError(response: Response): Promise<LlmError> {
  const requestId = response.headers.get('x-request-id')
  const detail = (await response.text().catch(() => '')).slice(0, 500)
  const options = {
    status: response.status,
    ...(requestId ? { requestId: ProviderRequestId(requestId) } : {}),
    ...(response.status === 429 ? { providerRetryAfterMs: retryAfterMs(response.headers) } : {}),
  }
  if (isHttpContextOverflow(response.status, detail)) return new LlmError(`Codex context window exceeded: ${detail}`, CONTEXT_OVERFLOW_CODE, options)
  if (response.status === 401) return new LlmError('ChatGPT sign-in has expired. Sign in again.', 'AUTH', options)
  if (response.status === 404) return new LlmError(`Codex model or resource not found (${response.status})${detail ? `: ${detail}` : '.'}`, 'NOT_FOUND', options)
  if (response.status === 429) return new LlmError('Codex rate limit reached.', 'RATE_LIMIT', options)
  if (response.status >= 500) return new LlmError(`Codex service error (${response.status}).`, 'SERVER_ERROR', options)
  return new LlmError(`Codex request failed (${response.status})${detail ? `: ${detail}` : '.'}`, 'PROVIDER_ERROR', options)
}

/**
 * Concatenated assistant text a non-delta `message` output item carries, which
 * the terminal events repeat. Empty for every other item type.
 * @param item - one \`output\` item from a Response.
 * @returns the item's output text, or an empty string.
 */
function messageItemText(item: Record<string, unknown> | null): string {
  if (item === null || string(item.type) !== 'message' || !Array.isArray(item.content)) return ''
  let text = ''
  for (const part of item.content) {
    const value = record(part)
    const kind = string(value?.type)
    if (kind !== 'output_text' && kind !== 'refusal') continue
    text += string(value?.text) ?? ''
  }
  return text
}

function record(value: unknown): Record<string, unknown> | null {
  return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value)
    ? value as Record<string, unknown>
    : null
}

function string(value: unknown): string | undefined {
  return typeof value === 'string' ? value : undefined
}

function number(value: unknown): number | undefined {
  const parsed = Number(value)
  return Number.isFinite(parsed) ? parsed : undefined
}

function acceptIdentity(current: string, incoming: unknown): string {
  return typeof incoming === 'string' && incoming.length > 0 ? incoming : current
}

 * Which store holds a provider line's account pool.

 *   macOS, the Secret Service on Linux. Every existing install has this, and
 *   nobody who never touches the setting sees a change.
 * - `credentials` — DSH's own credential store, through `ctx.credentials`. The
 *   option a server install should use: no external daemon, one store for every

 * let one pool move between two stores depending on whether a daemon happened to
 * answer, and a pool that moves looks exactly like a pool whose accounts were
 * lost. A wrong choice is reported instead — the card names the store in use, says

import { MacKeychainCredentialStore } from '../token-store-macos.ts'
import { SecretServiceCredentialStore } from '../credential-store-secret-service.ts'
import { WindowsDpapiCredentialStore } from '../token-store-windows.ts'
import { CorruptStoredDocumentError, type CredentialStore } from '../token-store.ts'
import { credentialsRecordKey, type CredentialsRecordSeam } from './credentials-compat.ts'
import type {
  PoolStorageBackend,
  PoolStorageDto,
  PoolStorageMode,
  PoolStorageUnavailableReason,
} from '../../shared/contracts.ts'

/** Store a deployment gets when no `poolStorage` is configured anywhere. */
export const DEFAULT_POOL_STORAGE_MODE: PoolStorageMode = 'keyring'

/** Record scope the pool document occupies in DSH's credential store. */
const POOL_RECORD_SCOPE = 'dsh-chatgpt-subscription'

/**
 * Record id prefix for one pool: `<scope>/pool-<digest>`.
 *
 * The prefix is load-bearing, not decoration. The seam requires each key segment
 * to match `/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/` while a pool's id is a sha256 hex digest, and
 * 62.5% of digests start with a digit — those keys are rejected on the NEXT start,
 * when the record document is parsed, and an invalid key fails the whole provider's
 * activation: the DeepSeek key, the Telegram token and every other secret in
 * `$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml` become unreadable. `pool-` puts a letter first and
 * leaves the digest untouched, so the address stays stable and the Secret Service
 * entry (which uses the bare digest as its account attribute) is unaffected.
 */
function poolRecordKey(account: string): string {
  return credentialsRecordKey(POOL_RECORD_SCOPE, `pool-${account}`)
}

/**
 * The deployment-wide choice, as the runtime sees it.
 *
 * One plugin instance serves every provider line and one profile carries one
 * `poolStorage`, so the value is read where the lines are built and consulted
 * here. Module state rather than a constructor argument on eleven pools: a
 * parameter would have to be threaded through ten provider constructors (one of
 * which takes no options at all) to describe one deployment-wide decision.
 */
export interface PoolStorageDefaults {
  /** Where the configured value comes from; read on every resolve. */
  mode?: () => PoolStorageMode
  /** Awaited before the mode is read, so a choice stored on disk is in place. */
  ready?: () => Promise<void>
  /**
   * `ctx.credentials`, read on EVERY resolve rather than captured once.
   *
   * A getter because the service is deliberately not in `inject`: nothing orders
   * it before this plugin's `apply`, and a value captured there would send every
   * pool of the process down the "no ctx.credentials service" branch for the rest
   * of the process's life — `poolStorage: 'credentials'` reporting an unusable
   * store on a host that has one.
   */
  credentials?: () => CredentialsRecordSeam | undefined
  logger?: Pick<Console, 'info' | 'warn'>
}

let defaults: PoolStorageDefaults = { mode: () => DEFAULT_POOL_STORAGE_MODE }

 * Revision of the deployment-wide choice.
 *
 * Every resolved pool remembers the revision it resolved under and re-resolves
 * when this moves. Without it, switching the store in the settings card would keep
 * serving the old backend until the host restarted: the resolution is deliberately
 * cached — the decision must not be retaken per request — so the switch has to
 * invalidate it explicitly.
 */
let revision = 0

/** Record the deployment-wide storage choice; call once, before any pool is built. */
export function configurePoolStorage(next: PoolStorageDefaults): void {
  defaults = next.mode === undefined ? { ...next, mode: () => DEFAULT_POOL_STORAGE_MODE } : next
  revision += 1
}

/**
 * Announce that the stored choice changed.
 *
 * Called by the settings route after the new value is on disk; every pool drops
 * the backend it cached and resolves again on its next read.
 */
export function poolStorageChanged(): void {
  revision += 1
}

/** The revision the current choice stands at. */
export function poolStorageRevision(): number {
  return revision
}

/** The configured mode, without resolving a backend. */
export function poolStorageMode(): PoolStorageMode {
  return defaults.mode?.() ?? DEFAULT_POOL_STORAGE_MODE
}

/** Clear the deployment-wide choice, so one test cannot leak into the next. */
export function resetPoolStorage(): void {
  defaults = { mode: () => DEFAULT_POOL_STORAGE_MODE }
  revision += 1
}

  keyring?: ProbeableKeyringStore<T>

export interface PoolStorageResolution<T> {
  store: CredentialStore<T>
  storage: PoolStorageDto
}

const BACKEND_LABELS: Record<PoolStorageBackend, string> = {
  keyring: 'desktop keyring (Secret Service)',
  credentials: 'DSH credential store',
  dpapi: 'Windows DPAPI',
  keychain: 'macOS Keychain',
}

/** Human label of one backend, for the log line and for diagnostics. */
export function poolStorageBackendLabel(backend: PoolStorageBackend): string {
  return BACKEND_LABELS[backend]
}

/** Whether the backend encrypts the document at rest. */
export function poolStorageEncrypted(backend: PoolStorageBackend): boolean {
  return backend === 'keyring' || backend === 'dpapi' || backend === 'keychain'
}

/**
 * The pool document as a record in DSH's own credential store.
 *
 * Stored through the seam's record half (see `credentials-compat.ts`): the
 * document is this plugin's own format, and a `grant` payload is exactly the slot
 * the seam keeps for a value only its owner can interpret.
 *
 * Writes are LAST-WRITER-WINS, and honestly so. `modifyRecord` is the seam's only
 * write path and it does hand back the record as it stands under its lock, but a
 * whole pool document is written from one in-memory copy: a second process that
 * saved between this process's read and this write is overwritten. The lock makes
 * the write atomic, not the transaction. This is the same guarantee the keyring
 * backend has always given, and exactly what the `keyring` option gives — one
 * process is the normal case (one `DSH_HOME`, one host), and it is stated here
 * rather than implied away.
 */
export class CredentialsRecordStore<T> implements CredentialStore<T> {
  constructor(
    private readonly seam: CredentialsRecordSeam,
    private readonly key: string,
    private readonly parse: (value: unknown) => T,
  ) {}

  /** The `<scope>/<id>` address this pool occupies; a location, never a credential. */
  recordKey(): string {
    return this.key
  }

  async load(): Promise<T | null> {
    const record = await this.seam.readRecord(this.key)
    if (record === undefined) return null
    if (record.kind !== 'grant') throw new CorruptStoredDocumentError('pool record is not a grant')
    try {
      return this.parse(record.payload)
    } catch (error) {
      // Typed as CORRUPT, not unavailable: a document that does not parse is what
      // the next write repairs, while a seam that did not answer must not be
      // treated as an empty pool.
      throw new CorruptStoredDocumentError('DSH credential store pool payload is invalid', { cause: error })
    }
  }

  async save(value: T): Promise<void> {
    // The seam promises the payload survives a JSON round trip and nothing more,
    // so the document is normalized to plain JSON BEFORE it is handed over: a
    // field of `undefined` inside it would otherwise vanish on read-back and make
    // the pool's own write verification fail on a save that actually succeeded.
    const payload = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value)) as unknown
    // `current` is deliberately not merged: this class holds one pool document and
    // the caller owns its contents, so the load-modify-save it performs is the
    // merge. Writing back the record as it stood would resurrect accounts this
    // process has just deleted. See the class comment for the scope of the lock.
    await this.seam.modifyRecord(this.key, async () => ({ kind: 'grant', payload }))
  }

  async clear(): Promise<void> {
    await this.seam.deleteRecord(this.key)
  }
}

/**
 * A backend that cannot be used on this host, kept so the failure is reported with
 * its reason instead of being replaced by a silent substitution.
 *
 * `poolStorage` is an instruction. Answering it with a different store would make
 * the settings card describe a backend the user did not choose, and — worse —
 * would spread one deployment's accounts across two stores without saying so.
 * Every operation therefore fails with the sentence the card also shows, and
 * `unavailable` tells the card which reason code to translate.
 */
class UnusablePoolStore<T> implements CredentialStore<T> {
  constructor(private readonly message: string) {}

  async load(): Promise<T | null> {
    throw new Error(this.message)
  }

  async save(): Promise<void> {
    throw new Error(this.message)
  }

  async clear(): Promise<void> {
    throw new Error(this.message)
  }
}

/** What the user is told when `keyring` is configured and there is no keyring. */
const KEYRING_UNREACHABLE = 'poolStorage is "keyring", but this host has no reachable desktop keyring: '
  + 'the Secret Service does not answer (no secret-tool, no session bus, or a locked keyring). '
  + 'Switch "Account storage" to the DSH credential store, or set poolStorage: "credentials".'

/** What the user is told when `credentials` is configured and the harness has no such seam. */
const NO_CREDENTIALS_SERVICE = 'poolStorage is "credentials", but this harness has no ctx.credentials service, '
  + 'so there is no DSH credential store to write into. Switch "Account storage" to the desktop keyring, '
  + 'or set poolStorage: "keyring".'

/**
 * Resolve the pool store for one line.
 *
 * Async because `credentials` availability is a runtime fact and the configured
 * value may still be loading from disk; callers hold the promise rather than the
 * store (see `AccountPoolCore`).
 */
export async function resolvePoolStorage<T>(request: PoolStorageRequest<T>): Promise<PoolStorageResolution<T>> {
  const platform = request.platform ?? process.platform
  const logger = request.logger ?? defaults.logger ?? console
  await defaults.ready?.()
  const mode = request.mode ?? defaults.mode?.() ?? DEFAULT_POOL_STORAGE_MODE
  const seam = request.credentials ?? defaults.credentials?.()

  if (mode === 'credentials') {
    if (seam === undefined) {
      logger.warn(`[dsh-chatgpt-subscription] ${NO_CREDENTIALS_SERVICE}`)
      return unusable<T>(mode, 'credentials', 'no-credentials-service', NO_CREDENTIALS_SERVICE)
    }
    const store = new CredentialsRecordStore(
      seam,
      poolRecordKey(request.account),
      request.parsePoolData,
    )
    logger.info(`[dsh-chatgpt-subscription] account pool stored in ${BACKEND_LABELS.credentials}`)
    return resolved(store, mode, 'credentials')
  }

  // `keyring`: the platform store — a different store on each platform, and
  // exactly what it was before this option existed.
  if (platform === 'win32' || platform === 'darwin') {
    const backend: PoolStorageBackend = platform === 'win32' ? 'dpapi' : 'keychain'
    const store = request.desktopStore ?? (platform === 'win32'
      ? new WindowsDpapiCredentialStore(`${request.poolFile}.dpapi`, request.parsePoolData)
      : new MacKeychainCredentialStore(request.keychainService, request.account, request.parsePoolData))
    logger.info(`[dsh-chatgpt-subscription] account pool stored in ${BACKEND_LABELS[backend]}`)
    return resolved(store, mode, backend)
  }
  if (platform !== 'linux') {
    throw new Error(`${request.displayName} pool storage requires Windows, macOS, or Linux.`)
  }

  const keyring = request.keyring
    ?? new SecretServiceCredentialStore(request.keychainService, request.account, request.parsePoolData)
  const availability = await probeKeyring(keyring)
  if (!availability.available) {
    // No silent fallback: the user asked for the keyring, so a save has to fail
    // with the sentence that says what to change, instead of succeeding in a store
    // they did not choose and cannot see from the card.
    const reason = availability.reason === undefined
      ? KEYRING_UNREACHABLE
      : `${KEYRING_UNREACHABLE} (${availability.reason})`
    logger.warn(`[dsh-chatgpt-subscription] ${reason}`)
    return unusable<T>(mode, 'keyring', 'keyring-unreachable', reason)
  }
  logger.info(`[dsh-chatgpt-subscription] account pool stored in ${BACKEND_LABELS.keyring}`)
  return resolved(keyring, mode, 'keyring')
}

/**
 * The store a caller-supplied backend stands in for, on this platform.
 *
 * `AccountPoolHooks.backend` replaces the STORE, not the choice, and adoption
 * harnesses use it without a `storage` to go with it. Falling back to
 * `{ backend: 'keyring', encrypted: false }` there described a backend that cannot
 * exist (the platform keyring is encrypted on every platform it exists on) and the
 * wrong one on Windows or macOS.
 */
export function poolStorageBackendForPlatform(platform: NodeJS.Platform): PoolStorageBackend {
  if (platform === 'win32') return 'dpapi'
  if (platform === 'darwin') return 'keychain'
  return 'keyring'
}

function resolved<T>(
  store: CredentialStore<T>,
  mode: PoolStorageMode,
  backend: PoolStorageBackend,
): PoolStorageResolution<T> {
  return { store, storage: { mode, backend, encrypted: poolStorageEncrypted(backend) } }
}

function unusable<T>(
  mode: PoolStorageMode,
  backend: PoolStorageBackend,
  unavailable: PoolStorageUnavailableReason,
  message: string,
): PoolStorageResolution<T> {
  return {
    store: new UnusablePoolStore<T>(`ChatGPT account pool storage is unavailable: ${message}`),
    storage: { mode, backend, encrypted: poolStorageEncrypted(backend), unavailable },
  }
}

/** Whether the keyring answers at all; a backend without a probe is assumed to. */
async function probeKeyring<T>(keyring: ProbeableKeyringStore<T>): Promise<{ available: boolean; reason?: string }> {
  if (typeof keyring.ping !== 'function') return { available: true }
  return keyring.ping()
}

/**
 * Human description of where a resolved pool lives, for diagnostics.
 *
 * A location, never a credential: the sentence the pool printed before, now
 * derived from the backend that actually won.
 */
export function describePoolStoragePath(
  platform: NodeJS.Platform,
  poolFile: string,
  storage: PoolStorageDto,
  keychainService: string,
  account: string,
): string {
  if (storage.backend === 'dpapi') return `${poolFile}.dpapi`
  if (storage.backend === 'credentials') return `credentials://${poolRecordKey(account)}`
  return `${platform === 'darwin' ? 'Keychain' : 'Secret Service'}: ${keychainService}/${account}`
}

const DIRECTORY_MODE = 0o700
const FILE_MODE = 0o600

export function defaultLinuxCredentialPath(): string {

/**
 * Linux credential storage protected by owner-only filesystem permissions.
 * The payload is not encrypted at rest, so callers must report that distinction
 * instead of presenting this store as equivalent to Windows DPAPI.
 */
export class LinuxFileTokenStore implements TokenStore {
  readonly storage = { kind: 'linux-file', encrypted: false } as const
  private readonly noFollow = constants.O_NOFOLLOW

  constructor(private readonly path = defaultLinuxCredentialPath()) {
    if (process.platform !== 'linux') throw new Error('Linux credential storage requires Linux')
    if (this.noFollow === undefined) throw new Error('Linux credential storage requires O_NOFOLLOW support')
    if (dirname(path) === path) throw new Error('invalid Linux credential path')
  }

  async load(): Promise<StoredOAuthCredentials | null> {
    let handle
    try {
      handle = await open(this.path, constants.O_RDONLY | this.noFollow)
    } catch (error) {
      if (isMissing(error)) return null
      throw new Error('Linux credential read failed', { cause: error })
    }

    try {
      const stats = await handle.stat()
      if (!stats.isFile()) throw new Error('credential path is not a regular file')
      if (typeof process.getuid === 'function' && stats.uid !== process.getuid()) {
        throw new Error('credential file is owned by another user')
      }
      if ((stats.mode & 0o777) !== FILE_MODE) {
        throw new Error('credential file permissions must be 0600')
      }
      const payload = await handle.readFile({ encoding: 'utf8' })
      return parseStoredCredentials(JSON.parse(payload) as unknown)
    } catch (error) {
      // A document that does not parse (or a file whose ownership / mode is
      // wrong) is corrupt data, not an unreachable store: the pool may repair it
      // with a write, and must not treat the read as "no accounts".
      throw new CorruptStoredDocumentError('Linux credential payload is invalid or insecure', { cause: error })
    } finally {
      await handle.close()
    }
  }

  async save(value: StoredOAuthCredentials): Promise<void> {
    const directory = dirname(this.path)
    const temporary = `${this.path}.tmp-${randomUUID()}`
    try {
      const existing = await lstat(this.path)
      if (existing.isSymbolicLink() || !existing.isFile()) {
        throw new Error('credential path is not a regular file')
      }
      assertOwnedByCurrentUser(existing.uid, 'credential file')
    } catch (error) {
      if (!isMissing(error)) throw new Error('Linux credential write failed', { cause: error })
    }
    await mkdir(directory, { recursive: true, mode: DIRECTORY_MODE })
    const directoryStats = await stat(directory)
    if (!directoryStats.isDirectory()) throw new Error('Linux credential directory is invalid')
    assertOwnedByCurrentUser(directoryStats.uid, 'credential directory')
    await chmod(directory, DIRECTORY_MODE)

    let handle
    try {
      handle = await open(temporary, constants.O_WRONLY | constants.O_CREAT | constants.O_EXCL, FILE_MODE)
      await handle.writeFile(JSON.stringify(value), { encoding: 'utf8' })
      await handle.sync()
      await handle.close()
      handle = undefined
      await rename(temporary, this.path)
      await chmod(this.path, FILE_MODE)
    } catch (error) {
      await handle?.close().catch(() => undefined)
      await unlink(temporary).catch(() => undefined)
      throw new Error('Linux credential write failed', { cause: error })
    }
  }

  async clear(): Promise<void> {
    try {
      await unlink(this.path)
    } catch (error) {
      if (isMissing(error)) return
      throw new Error('Linux credential deletion failed', { cause: error })
    }
  }
}

function assertOwnedByCurrentUser(owner: number, label: string): void {
  if (typeof process.getuid === 'function' && owner !== process.getuid()) {
    throw new Error(`${label} is owned by another user`)
  }
}

function isMissing(error: unknown): boolean {
  return typeof error === 'object' && error !== null && 'code' in error && error.code === 'ENOENT'
}
